title: A Lion's Roar Can Be Heard 5 Miles Away (It's 114 Decibels)

scenes.text: A lion's roar can be heard five miles away.
Up close it's 114 decibels. Twenty-five times louder than a lawn mower.
A roar isn't one blast. It comes in bouts, around 50 roars in 90 seconds.
The secret is in its throat. Most animals have triangular vocal folds. A lion's are flat and square, padded with fat.
That shape lets the folds flap hard on very little air. Maximum noise for minimum breath.
Five miles. Every lion in that radius just got the message.

description:
A lion's roar can carry about five miles across the savanna. Measured a few feet away it reaches around 114 decibels, which researchers compared to 25 times the loudness of a petrol lawn mower.
A 2011 study found the secret in the larynx: lions and tigers have flat, square vocal folds padded with fat, so they can roar extremely loudly using surprisingly little lung pressure, in bouts of about 50 roars over 90 seconds.
Lion roar or thunder: which would scare you more at night? Comment below.
first_comment: The researchers said a lion's roar works a lot like a baby's cry: loose, irregular vocal folds make both sound rough and impossible to ignore. What is the loudest animal you have heard in real life?
